fact_check_verdict: GO WITH ATTRIBUTION AND SCOPE LIMITS

claims.spoken: Koniag Government Services posted its announcement on September 11th.
requires: This is the company page announcement date, not a launch date, award date or new contract.

claims.spoken: KGS says it supports the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office on Wingman.
requires: Attribute support to KGS. Name CDAO as Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office; do not call it the Army CDAO.
claims.label: Koniag Government Services

claims.spoken: KGS is a subsidiary of Koniag.
requires: Parent investments page describes the portfolio as subsidiary companies; the portfolio names KGS under government contracting. Corporate ownership, not tribal-government operation.

claims.spoken: Koniag is the regional Alaska Native corporation associated with the Kodiak region.
requires: Name Koniag as the regional corporation. Do not conflate KGS, Koniag, individual shareholders, or tribal governments. No Native culture imagery or characterization.

claims.spoken: Wingman supports custom digital assistants for repetitive office work.
requires: This is the announced platform purpose, not audited output quality or a new deployment count. Restrict visualization to documents and clerical office workflows.

claims.spoken: KGS names contracting, logistics and financial management among the workflows.
requires: Named workflow categories only. Do not imply every process is deployed, succeeds or runs without review.

claims.spoken: Earlier Army procurement work included DORA, the Determination of Responsibility Assistant.
requires: Introduce this as earlier Army procurement work described in the AWS vendor case study; do not frame it as a new September 11th launch.

claims.spoken: A contracting professional emails a vendor identifier in the subject line.
requires: The identifier is a Unique Entity Identifier, or UEI. Use a generic labeled token; no real vendor record, contact or invented valid identifier.

claims.spoken: DORA retrieves compliance data through APIs, including SAM.gov data.
requires: Show documented data retrieval. Do not invent which additional databases are queried or imply direct access to private tax returns.

claims.spoken: Prebuilt decision logic helps assemble a standardized report.
requires: DORA uses prebuilt decisioning algorithms. This is distinct from the separately described generative drafting tools. Do not visualize a language model inventing compliance evidence.

claims.spoken: The report goes to a professional for review and determination.
requires: A human contracting professional remains responsible for review and determination. No automatic award or guaranteed legal-compliance claim.

claims.spoken: Separate Jumpstarter tools use large language models through Amazon Bedrock.
requires: Keep generative drafting distinct from DORA data and rules automation. Identify the tools as earlier Army work, not newly measured Wingman results.

claims.spoken: Users provide inputs to produce first drafts of contracting documents.
requires: A first draft is not a final contract, approval or award. Depict draft status persistently on every generated document.

claims.spoken: People refine and approve the generated sections.
requires: This is the KGS-described workflow in the AWS case study, not independently audited accuracy. Keep the professional visible after drafting.

claims.spoken: AWS reports that the DORA task fell from roughly an hour to two minutes.
requires: OPTIONAL. If used, attribute in the same spoken span to AWS and visibly to AWS CASE STUDY. Limit to the DORA responsibility-check task in earlier Army procurement work. The duration of human review is not separately established. Never expand it to the whole procurement or award.
claims.label: AWS vendor case study
claims.verbatim_source: By reducing a one-hour task to just 2 minutes

claims.spoken: AWS reports about 37 million dollars in annual cost avoidance across the earlier Army automation portfolio.
requires: OPTIONAL. If used, say ABOUT and ANNUAL COST AVOIDANCE, visibly name the Army portfolio, and attribute to AWS. KGS release says more than $37M for earlier Army work. These are related vendor reports, not independent audits. Never Wingman-only, DORA-only, profit, cash savings, Alaska revenue or shareholder distributions.
claims.label: AWS vendor case study

claims.spoken: AWS reports 687,000 labor hours saved annually across the Army automation portfolio.
requires: OPTIONAL. If used, attribute to AWS and visibly scope to the broader Army automation portfolio. Body states 687,000 in two locations; headline contains typo 687,00. Do not reproduce the typo, extrapolate jobs, or assign all hours to DORA or Wingman.
claims.label: AWS vendor case study

claims.spoken: The announcement gives no Wingman contract value or quantified Alaska return.
requires: Scope absence to this announcement. No inference of no benefit, no jobs or no contract. Do not turn Army cost avoidance into money flowing to Alaska.

kill_list: New September 11th Wingman launch or contract award
Any quantified Alaska jobs, cash return or shareholder distribution
DORA or Wingman alone saved the broader Army portfolio totals
An entire procurement or contract award takes two minutes
AI alone produced every reported saving
DORA is the generative Jumpstarter model
Tribal-government operation or Native culture imagery
limitations: GO only for the fresh attributed company announcement and separately labeled earlier Army clerical-workflow example.
The KGS-hosted AWS case study reproduces the AWS account. Cross-host agreement is not independent performance validation.
No independent government performance audit or second independent primary source for DORA timing was located. Optional performance figures must remain vendor-attributed or be cut.
AWS body supports 687,000, while its headline has 687,00. Do not infer precision, jobs, cash recovered, or Wingman-specific savings.
No Wingman contract value, local deployment, Alaska jobs, shareholder distribution, independent accuracy rate, or new launch date is established by the announcement.
The first-person source framing of corporate identity must not become tribal-government, pan-Native, cultural or community sentiment claims.
No military operational capability, targeting, weapons, battlefield outcome or protected-data claim is approved.
DORA is described through APIs and prebuilt decision logic; only the separate Jumpstarter tools have an explicit LLM/generative drafting mechanism.

Current claims_contract_check.py does not enforce on_screen_none or conditional_display_contract. It also checks on_screen_all unconditionally even when must_ship is false. Final source-route, narration and rendered visual review must enforce negative and conditional obligations.
The AWS account labels CDAO imprecisely as an Army office. Use Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office without the Army qualifier, following the fresh KGS release.
quote_policy: No quotation selected for narration. The short verbatim_source timing fragment exists only to verify optional c15. Paraphrase all approved spoken copy.
